subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the MXC lifecycle-status bug is fixed, should OpenClaw accept the exact-head native MXC dependency graph and the upstream `--config-base64` argv transport boundary for this prerelease Windows sandbox plugin?
rationale: Automation can identify the code-level lifecycle bug, but accepting a first-party sandbox backend with native executor binaries, `node-pty` install-time code, and process-argv config exposure is a maintainer/security boundary decision.

options.title: Approve after lifecycle fix
options.body: Fix the stale runtime status first, then approve dependency-guard on the exact current SHA if security owners accept the MXC SDK and argv transport boundary.

options.title: Pause for safer transport
options.body: Hold the PR until upstream MXC provides a non-argv config transport or OpenClaw has an accepted reduced-exposure design.

options.title: Incubate outside first-party release
options.body: Keep MXC as an independently published experimental plugin until the dependency and sandbox lifecycle boundary is mature enough for OpenClaw-owned release metadata.

recommendation.title: Approve after lifecycle fix
recommendation.body: Fix the stale runtime status first, then approve dependency-guard on the exact current SHA if security owners accept the MXC SDK and argv transport boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The live PR is assigned to `steipete`, and he is the strongest available routing owner for the release/security acceptance choice.
